title: What can you say about passionflower in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 2 wordings for passionflower; the strongest is "Traditionally used in herbal medicine to help relieve restlessness or nervousness" (limited, 0.25-8 g dried herb top (or extract equivalent) a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats insomnia".

supported_wordings.wording: Traditionally used in herbal medicine to help relieve restlessness or nervousness.
supported_wordings.why: Traditional use in Health Canada's monograph; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.daily_dose: 0.25-8 g dried herb top (or extract equivalent) a day
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adolescents 12 to 17 and adults. Water extracts (decoction, infusion, aqueous dry extract) start at 1 g a day.
supported_wordings.form: Dried herb top, powder or extracts

supported_wordings.wording: Traditionally used in herbal medicine as a sleep aid for occasional sleeplessness during times of mental stress.
supported_wordings.why: Traditional use in Health Canada's monograph; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.daily_dose: 0.25-8 g dried herb top (or extract equivalent) a day
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adolescents 12 to 17 and adults. Water extracts (decoction, infusion, aqueous dry extract) start at 1 g a day. Take 1 hour before bedtime as needed. Health Canada asks people to see a practitioner if sleeplessness lasts more than 4 weeks.
supported_wordings.form: Dried herb top, powder or extracts

wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a sleep disorder; Health Canada says sleeplessness lasting more than 4 weeks needs a practitioner.
Names a mental health disorder; the supported wording is restlessness or nervousness.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Works like a sleeping pill or a benzodiazepine
wordings_to_avoid.why: Compares the product to a drug.
FDA's 2000 rule (page 1031) says help falling asleep implies treating insomnia unless the context makes clear the product is only for occasional sleeplessness.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

sources.name: FDA final rule on structure/function statements, 65 FR 1000 (6 January 2000), page 1031

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
